status_as_of_cutoff: Official Google/state announcement plus Haskell County tax-abatement records and TDLR architectural-barriers filings now confirm named Haskell County data-center projects and Armstrong County data-center filings at the announced county level; no public official source found for energized status or project-level IT capacity.
evidence_grade: A- for announced Google Texas program and Haskell County/TDLR filings; B for Armstrong/Goodnight linkage to Google's announced Armstrong campus because TDLR owner is GN DC1 LLC/Crusoe affiliate and tenant is not disclosed in the state filings.

actions.body: Office of the Governor of Texas
actions.result_or_status: Governor's release announced Google's planned $40 billion Texas investment and new data-center campuses; it is not a county permit, zoning decision, or vote.
actions.access_caveat: Official state announcement, not an approval docket; county locations and permits were not attached.

actions.result_or_status: Google announced a $40 billion Texas investment through 2027 for cloud and AI infrastructure, including new data center campuses in Armstrong and Haskell Counties, plus energy initiatives.
actions.access_caveat: Company announcement; does not disclose site parcels, permits, energized status, or data-center MW.
actions.notes: Google separately says it has contracted more than 6,200 MW of new energy generation/capacity in Texas, but that is not a data-center capacity figure.

actions.result_or_status: Google's Texas data-center location page lists existing Ellis County locations in Midlothian and Red Oak and says the November 2025 investment includes new data-center campuses in Armstrong, Haskell, Pampa and Wilbarger Counties.
actions.access_caveat: Company page; current as crawled during refresh but not a county permit docket.
actions.notes: Pampa/Wilbarger are adjacent/newer Google Texas items and are not folded into this center's county list except as context.

actions.result_or_status: County tax-abatement page lists Homebound Data Center - Thelma (Google), Homebound Group, LLC - Journey (Google), and Homebound Group, LLC - Quest (Google), each dated June 24, 2025.
actions.access_caveat: County page links agreements but this refresh relied on the public listing text; individual agreement PDFs were not parsed.
actions.notes: This is the strongest local-government source tying Haskell Homebound projects to Google.

actions.body: Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation
actions.result_or_status: TABS2025019833 registered Data Center THM1A / Data Center 1 at 10357 Loop Road, Haskell County; new construction; 280,000 sq ft; estimated cost $350 million; start date 2025-06-18; completion date 2027-04-16; owner Homebound Group LLC; status Project Registered.
actions.access_caveat: TDLR architectural-barriers filing; not a certificate of occupancy or energized-status record.
actions.notes: Matches Haskell County's Thelma/Homebound Google abatement context.

actions.body: Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation

actions.access_caveat: TDLR architectural-barriers filing; not a certificate of occupancy or energized-status record.

actions.body: Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation
actions.result_or_status: TABS2025026455 and TABS2025026470 registered Llano Buildings 1 and 2 at 10001 Lima Rd, Claude, Armstrong County; each is a 484,954 sq ft one-story data center with estimated cost $292 million and start date 2025-08-25; owner GN DC1 LLC.
actions.access_caveat: TDLR filings do not disclose tenant; Google linkage is inferred from Google's announced Armstrong County campus plus regional reporting on Goodnight/Llano.
actions.notes: Building 1 status Review Complete; Building 2 status Project Registered. Building 2 URL: https://www.tdlr.texas.gov/TABS/Projects/TABS2025026470

contradictions: Official Google sources confirm Armstrong and Haskell County campuses but do not disclose site addresses or data-center MW; Haskell County directly labels Homebound Thelma/Journey/Quest as Google, while Armstrong TDLR filings list GN DC1 LLC and no tenant.

Google's 6,200 MW figure is contracted Texas energy generation/capacity, not official data-center IT/load capacity. Third-party estimates for Goodnight/Armstrong exceed 1 GW but are not entered as capacity_mw.
